scheme_name: Chief Minister’s Girl Child Protection Scheme-I
description:
The Chief Minister’s Girl Child Protection Scheme-I was launched by the Government of Haryana on 1st January 2016. 

This scheme was initiated to address the declining sex ratio in the state of Haryana. 

The sex ratio in Haryana was reported to be 877 girls for every 1,000 boys as per the 2011 Census. 

This alarming figure highlighted the need for targeted interventions to promote the welfare of the girl child. 

The primary objective of the scheme is to improve the sex ratio and ensure the protection and empowerment of the girl child. 

The scheme aims to provide financial assistance to families for the education and health of their girl children. 

The government has set a measurable target to increase the sex ratio to 950 girls for every 1,000 boys by the year 2025. 

Under this scheme, a total financial assistance of INR 21,000 is provided for each girl child. 

The assistance is disbursed in installments at various stages of the girl child's life. 

The first installment of INR 5,000 is provided at the time of the birth of the girl child. 

The second installment of INR 5,000 is given when the girl child reaches the age of one year. 

The third installment of INR 5,000 is provided when the girl child is enrolled in the first grade of school. 

The fourth installment of INR 6,000 is released when the girl child reaches the age of 18 years. 

This structured financial support aims to encourage families to invest in the education and health of their daughters. 

Eligibility for the scheme is restricted to families with a maximum annual income of INR 2.5 lakh. 

The scheme is applicable to families that have a girl child born on or after 1st January 2016. 

The scheme is open to all families residing in Haryana, irrespective of their caste or community. 

To apply for the scheme, parents or guardians must submit an application form to the concerned department. 

The application form can be obtained from the office of the Child Development Project Officer or downloaded from the official website. 

Along with the application form, the following documents are required: 

1. Birth certificate of the girl child.
2. Income certificate of the family.
3. Aadhar card of the parents or guardians.
4. Bank account details for the disbursement of funds.
5. Passport-sized photographs of the girl child.

Once the application is submitted, it is verified by the concerned authorities. 

The verification process typically takes about 30 days. 

After successful verification, the financial assistance is credited to the bank account provided in the application. 

The scheme is implemented by the Department of Women and Child Development, Haryana. 

The department is responsible for monitoring and evaluating the progress of the scheme. 

The Chief Minister’s Girl Child Protection Scheme-I is part of a broader initiative to empower women and girls in Haryana. 

The government has also launched various awareness campaigns to promote the importance of the girl child. 

These campaigns aim to change societal attitudes towards the girl child and promote gender equality. 

The scheme has received positive feedback from beneficiaries and has contributed to an increase in the birth rate of girl children. 

As of 2023, the sex ratio in Haryana has shown improvement, reaching 919 girls for every 1,000 boys. 

This improvement is attributed to the combined efforts of various government initiatives, including this scheme. 

The scheme has also encouraged families to prioritize the education of their daughters. 

Reports indicate that enrollment rates for girls in primary education have increased significantly since the launch of the scheme. 

The government has allocated a budget of INR 100 crore for the implementation of this scheme in the financial year 2022-2023. 

The scheme is expected to continue receiving financial support to ensure its sustainability. 

In addition to financial assistance, the scheme also emphasizes the importance of health check-ups for girl children. 

Regular health check-ups are encouraged to monitor the growth and development of the girl child. 

The scheme aims to create a supportive environment for the girl child through community engagement. 

Local self-governments and non-governmental organizations are also involved in promoting the scheme. 

The government conducts regular workshops and training sessions for parents to educate them about the benefits of the scheme. 

The Chief Minister’s Girl Child Protection Scheme-I is a significant step towards achieving gender equality in Haryana. 

It reflects the government's commitment to improving the status of women and girls in the state. 

The scheme is aligned with the national objectives of the Beti Bachao Beti Padhao initiative. 

This initiative aims to ensure the survival, protection, and education of the girl child across India. 

The success of the scheme is measured through regular assessments and feedback from beneficiaries. 

The government encourages beneficiaries to share their experiences to improve the scheme further. 

The Chief Minister’s Girl Child Protection Scheme-I is a vital component of Haryana's social welfare policies. 

It aims to create a future where every girl child is valued and empowered. 

The scheme has the potential to transform societal attitudes towards the girl child in Haryana. 

By providing financial support and promoting education, the scheme seeks to break the cycle of gender discrimination. 

The government is committed to ensuring that the benefits of the scheme reach the intended beneficiaries effectively. 

The Chief Minister’s Girl Child Protection Scheme-I exemplifies the proactive approach of the Haryana government towards women's empowerment. 

It serves as a model for other states in India to adopt similar initiatives for the welfare of the girl child. 

The scheme continues to evolve based on the changing needs of society and the feedback from its beneficiaries. 

Overall, the Chief Minister’s Girl Child Protection Scheme-I represents a significant investment in the future of girls in Haryana. 

It is a testament to the belief that empowering girls leads to the overall development of society.
